sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier with shining black frons and frontal shield, head capsule (including frontal shield, frons and postclypeus) almost uniformly smooth with very faint sculpture; anterior margin of the frontal shield straight, with only a narrow median notch; frontal shield raised but not projecting in lateral view, the frons forming 80° with the vertex; frontal horns prominent, hemispherical in lateral view, finger-like and diverging in dorsal view, genal horns small rounded tubercles appressed to the bases of the frontal horns. Alate uniformly yellowish brown, antennae 15—18 segments, mostly 17, segment formula 2=3>4=5; pronotum nearly square, almost as wide as the head width (including eyes). Known only from Little Cayman and western Jamaica.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body colour yellowish brown. Sclerotized veins pale brown, wing membrane very faintly smoky brown. Head yellowish brown, with a pale brown transverse band between the compound eyes. The yellowish brown chevron mark on the wing scales only weakly developed. Antennae and pronotum pale yellowish brown. Labrum and abdominal tergites yellowish brown. Femora nearly white, the rest of the legs including the tibiae yellowish brown. Sternites pale yellow. Head oval, coronal suture indistinct. Compound eyes large, protruding, oval, with a straight edge only along the antennal sockets. Ocelli medium-sized, oval, touching the compound eyes. Antennae 15—18 segments, mostly 17, formula usually 2=3>4=5, rarely 2=3=4=5 or 2>3=4=5. Pronotum nearly square, width nearly equal to the head width (including eyes); anterior margin shallowly concave, sides moderately convex, posterior margin slightly concave; transverse band and median line absent. Radius of forewing reaching half the distance from the wing base; radial sector with 6—7 branches. Arolium present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: In dorsal view the frons and frontal shield are shining black; in most specimens the anterior 1/3 to 1/2 of the vertex is also shining black, becoming chestnut-brown and rusty posteriorly in the posterior 1/3; in some specimens the region behind the frontal shield is dark chestnut-brown and the posterior part rusty orange or orange. In lateral view the frontal shield is nearly black, the posterior pigmentation rusty orange or rusty. Mandibles dark chestnut-brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum rusty, the rest of the thorax (including legs) and abdomen yellow to orange-yellow. Head capsule in dorsal view with sides nearly parallel, slightly constricted near the frontal shield, compound eyes usually very slightly protruding. Head (including frontal shield, frons and postclypeus) almost uniformly smooth and shining, sculpture very faint. Anterior margin of the frontal shield straight, with only a narrow median notch, the notch continuous with the vertex. Frontal concavity very shallow, nearly flat. Frontal shield raised (especially in lateral view) but not projecting. Frons forming 80° with the vertex. Labrum with a broad pointed apex and a small swelling at the tip. Frontal horns prominent: hemispherical in lateral view, oval in frontal view, finger-like and laterally diverging in dorsal view. Genal horns small rounded tubercles on the dorsum of the genae, appressed to the bases of the frontal horns. Mandibles sickle-shaped, medium length, broad at the base; apices upturned, covering the labrum and anteclypeus in frontal view. First marginal teeth of both mandibles short and pointed. Compound eyes prominent, large, oval. Antennae 11—16 segments, mostly 13 or 14; formula usually 2>3>4<5 or 2>3<4=5. Pronotum relatively long and narrow. Distribution: Little Cayman, western Jamaica; unknown elsewhere.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Geographic variation: soldiers of the Jamaican phenotype have a deeper concavity of the frons and frontal shield in dorsal view than specimens from Little Cayman. Type locality: Pirates' Point Resort, Little Cayman, Cayman Islands.
